58598-another-brownie-book.title: Brownie Book
58598-another-brownie-book.creator: Palmer Cox
58598-another-brownie-book.description: A book by Palmer Cox. When snowdrifts blocked the country roads,  And trees were bending with their loads,  The wind grew mild which had been raw,  And winter yielded to a thaw;  That night the Brownies stood to stare  In wonder on the village square. Said one, "This plot where drifts now roll  Seems like an acre from the Pole.

arxiv-2105-01814.title: On the minimal extension and structure of braided weakly group-theoretical fusion categories
arxiv-2105-01814.creator: Victor Ostrik, Zhiqiang Yu
arxiv-2105-01814.description: Abstract We show that any slightly degenerate weakly group-theoretical fusion category admits a minimal non-degenerate extension. Let d d be a positive square-free integer, given a weakly group-theoretical non-degenerate fusion category 𝒞 \mathcal{C} , assume that FPdim ​ ( 𝒞 ) = n ​ d \text{FPdim}(\mathcal{C})=nd and ( n , d ) = 1 (n,d)=1 .

arxiv-2112-00754.title: Integrability of the ν = 4 / 3 \nu=4/3 fractional quantum Hall edge states
arxiv-2112-00754.creator: Yichen Hu, Biao Lian
arxiv-2112-00754.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yichen Hu, Biao Lian. We investigate the homogeneous chiral edge theory of the filling ν = 4 / 3 \nu=4/3 fractional quantum Hall state, which is parameterized by a Luttinger liquid velocity matrix and an electron tunneling amplitude (ignoring irrelevant terms). We identify two solvable cases: one case where the theory gives two free chiral boson modes, and the other case where the theory yields one free charge 2 ​ e 3 \frac{2e}{\sqrt{3}} chiral fermion and two free chiral Bogoliubov (Majorana) fermions.

arxiv-2206-14579.title: Competence-based Multimodal Curriculum Learning for Medical Report Generation
arxiv-2206-14579.creator: Fenglin Liu, Shen Ge, Yuexian Zou, Xian Wu
arxiv-2206-14579.description: Abstract Medical report generation task, which targets to produce long and coherent descriptions of medical images, has attracted growing research interests recently. Different from the general image captioning tasks, medical report generation is more challenging for data-driven neural models. This is mainly due to 1) the serious data bias and 2) the limited medical data.

arxiv-2208-13356.title: Bounds on Irrationality Measures and the Flint-Hills Series
arxiv-2208-13356.creator: Alex Meiburg
arxiv-2208-13356.description: Abstract It is unknown whether the Flint-Hills series ∑ n = 1 ∞ 1 n 3 ​ sin 2 ⁡ ( n ) \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^{3}\sin^{2}(n)} converges. Alekseyev (2011) connected this question to the irrationality measure of π \pi , that μ ⁡ ( π ) > 5 2 \mu(\pi)>\frac{5}{2} would imply divergence of the Flint-Hills series.

arxiv-2306-01802.title: Linear Time GPs for Inferring Latent Trajectories from Neural Spike Trains
arxiv-2306-01802.creator: Matthew Dowling, Yuan Zhao, Il Memming Park
arxiv-2306-01802.description: Abstract Latent Gaussian process (GP) models are widely used in neuroscience to uncover hidden state evolutions from sequential observations, mainly in neural activity recordings. While latent GP models provide a principled and powerful solution in theory, the intractable posterior in non-conjugate settings necessitates approximate inference schemes, which may lack scalability.

arxiv-2306-05187.title: Safe Adaptive Multi-Agent Coverage Control
arxiv-2306-05187.creator: Yang Bai, Yujie Wang, Xiaogang Xiong, and Mikhail Svinin
arxiv-2306-05187.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yang Bai, Yujie Wang, Xiaogang Xiong, and Mikhail Svinin. This paper presents a safe adaptive coverage controller for multi-agent systems with actuator faults and time-varying uncertainties. The centroidal Voronoi tessellation (CVT) is applied to generate an optimal configuration of multi-agent systems for covering an area of interest.

arxiv-2410-04638.title: Provable Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Benign Overfitting
arxiv-2410-04638.creator: David X. Wu, Anant Sahai
arxiv-2410-04638.description: Abstract The classic teacher-student model in machine learning posits that a strong teacher supervises a weak student to improve the student’s capabilities. We instead consider the inverted situation, where a weak teacher supervises a strong student with imperfect pseudolabels. This paradigm was recently brought forth by Burns et al. (2023) and termed weak-to-strong generalization .

arxiv-2410-17506.title: Mitigating Graph Covariate Shift via Score-based Out-of-distribution Augmentation
arxiv-2410-17506.creator: Bohan Wang, Yurui Chang, Lu Lin
arxiv-2410-17506.description: Abstract Distribution shifts between training and testing datasets significantly impair the model performance on graph learning. A commonly-taken causal view in graph invariant learning suggests that stable predictive features of graphs are causally associated with labels, whereas varying environmental features lead to distribution shifts.

arxiv-2503-00811.title: Evaluating and Predicting Distorted Human Body Parts for Generated Images
arxiv-2503-00811.creator: Lu Ma * †, Kaibo Cao *, Hao Liang, Jiaxin Lin, Zhuang Li, Yuhong Liu, Jihong Zhang, Wentao Zhang ‡, Bin Cui ‡
arxiv-2503-00811.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lu Ma * †, Kaibo Cao *, Hao Liang, Jiaxin Lin, Zhuang Li, Yuhong Liu, Jihong Zhang, Wentao Zhang ‡, Bin Cui ‡. Recent advancements in text-to-image (T2I) models enable high-quality image synthesis, yet generating anatomically accurate human figures remains challenging. AI-generated images frequently exhibit distortions such as proliferated limbs, missing fingers, deformed extremities, or fused body parts.

arxiv-2503-20219.title: Multi-threaded Simulation Software for the JUNO Experiment
arxiv-2503-20219.creator: Y. Peng
arxiv-2503-20219.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Y. Peng. The Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) is a multi-purpose experiment under construction in southern China. JUNO aims to determine the neutrino mass ordering and precisely measure the neutrino oscillation parameters by detecting reactor neutrinos from nuclear power plants. In addition to reactor neutrinos, JUNO can study atmospheric neutrinos, solar neutrinos, geo-neutrinos, supernova burst neutrinos, the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background (DSNB), and nucleon decay, covering an energy range from keV to TeV.

arxiv-2507-19853.title: Spin-flop-like transition as quantum critical point in Cs 2 RuO 4
arxiv-2507-19853.creator: S.D. Nabi 1, M. Zhu 1, K. Yu. Povarov 2, D. G. Mazzone 3, J. Lass 3, Y. Wu 4, Z. Yan 1, S. Gvasaliya 1, A. Zheludev 1
arxiv-2507-19853.description: Abstract We report thermodynamic, neutron diffraction, and inelastic neutron scattering measurements on Cs 2 RuO 4 , a member of the celebrated family of frustrated magnets Cs M 2 ​ X 4 {}_{2}MX_{4} ( M M = Cu, Co, X X = Br, Cl).

arxiv-2509-11165.title: Traffic-MLLM: A Spatio-Temporal MLLM with Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Causal Inference in Traffic
arxiv-2509-11165.creator: Waikit Xiu, Qiang Lu, Xiying Li, Chen Hu, Shengbo Sun
arxiv-2509-11165.description: Abstract As intelligent transportation systems advance, traffic video understanding plays an increasingly pivotal role in comprehensive scene perception and causal analysis. Yet, existing approaches face notable challenges in accurately modeling spatiotemporal causality and integrating domain-specific knowledge, limiting their effectiveness in complex scenarios. To address these limitations, we propose Traffic-MLLM, a multimodal large language model tailored for fine-grained traffic analysis.

arxiv-2511-16897.title: Near-Optimal Dropout-Robust Sortition
arxiv-2511-16897.creator: Maya Pal Gambhir 1 , Bailey Flanigan 2 , Aaron Roth 1 1 University of Pennsylvania, 2 MIT
arxiv-2511-16897.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Maya Pal Gambhir 1 , Bailey Flanigan 2 , Aaron Roth 1 1 University of Pennsylvania, 2 MIT. Citizens’ assemblies – small panels of citizens that convene to deliberate on policy issues – often face the issue of panelists dropping out at the last-minute. Without intervention, these dropouts compromise the size and representativeness of the panel, prompting the question: Without seeing the dropouts ahead of time, can we choose panelists such that after dropouts, the panel will be representative and appropriately-sized?

pmc-10946052.creator: Shohei Ikeda, Koichi Sato, Morihiko Takeda, Mariko Shinozaki, Keita Miki, Michinori Hirano, Koji Fukuda, Nobuyuki Shiba
pmc-10946052.description: ObjectiveOncostatin M (OSM) is an inflammatory cytokine belonging to the interleukin-6 family member, which plays an important role in various cardiovascular diseases. We recently reported increased serum OSM levels in patients with coronary artery disease. However, the specific role in HF with ischemic heart disease (IHD) remains unclear.

pmc-11363959.title: Acupuncture indication knowledge bases: meridian entity recognition and classification based on ACUBERT
pmc-11363959.creator: TianCheng Xu, Jing Wen, Lei Wang, YueYing Huang, ZiJing Zhu, Qian Zhu, Yi Fang, ChengBiao Yang, YouBing Xia
pmc-11363959.description: In acupuncture diagnosis and treatment, non-quantitative clinical descriptions have limited the development of standardized treatment methods. This study explores the effectiveness and the reasons for discrepancies in the entity recognition and classification of meridians in acupuncture indication using the Acupuncture Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (ACUBERT) model.

pmc-11727083.title: Beta-Thalassemia and Male Infertility: Unraveling the Oxidative Stress Connection—An Up-to-Date Review
pmc-11727083.creator: Christos Roidos, Christos-Alexandros Batakoias, Evangelos N Symeonidis, Aris Kaltsas, Vasileios Tzikoulis, Georgios Tsampoukas, Chara Tsiampali, Natalia Palapela, Athanasios Zachariou, Nikolaos Sofikitis, Fotios Dimitriadis, Theo M de Reijke
pmc-11727083.description: Background/Objectives: Beta-thalassemia (BTH), a genetic disorder resulting from beta-globin gene mutations, affects over 1.5 million people globally. The disorder’s multifactorial impact on male fertility, particularly through oxidative stress (OS), warrants focused study. This review examines the mechanisms of OS in TM, its implications for male infertility, and the potential of antioxidant therapies to mitigate fertility challenges.

pmc-12506263.title: Evidence for reduced choroid plexus volume in the aged brain
pmc-12506263.creator: R Youh, C Perera, C Katsiva, I F Harrison, M F Lythgoe, D K Wright, S Nizari, Jack A Wells
pmc-12506263.description: BackgroundThe choroid plexus plays an important role in brain homeostasis, including the active secretion of cerebrospinal fluid. Its function and structure have been reported to be affected by normal ageing. However, existing measures of choroid plexus volume may be complicated by partial volume (in vivo MRI) and tissue fixation artefacts (histology).

pmc-12736125.title: Moving4notfrail®: A Rehabilitation Nursing Programme for Older Adults with Frailty
pmc-12736125.creator: Ana Isilda Torres Martins Santos, Ana da Conceição Alves Faria, Carla Gomes da Rocha, Abel Fernandes, Mariana Filipa Mendes Gonçalves, Joana Isabel Alves Quintas, Maria Narcisa da Costa Gonçalves, Olga Maria Pimenta Lopes Ribeiro, Richard Gray
pmc-12736125.description: Background/Objectives: Population ageing and the need for hospitalisation due to acute or chronic illness have contributed to increased physical frailty among older adults, with implications for their quality of life and healthcare. This study aims to describe the development and validation process of a rehabilitation nursing programme for hospitalised older adults experiencing physical frailty.

pmc-13052031.title: The Effect of Nursing Practice Environment, Individual and Occupational Characteristics on Nurses' Attitudes Towards Medical Error: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-13052031.creator: Şehrinaz Polat, Nilgün Göktepe, Begüm Yalçin, Emine Türkmen
pmc-13052031.description: AimThis study was conducted to examine the effect of nursing practice environment individual and occupational characteristics on nurses' attitudes towards medical error.DesignCross‐sectional study.MethodsThe questionnaire was used for data collection in a tertiary university hospital from 4 March to 30 April 2022. The questionnaire included the “Information Form”, the “Practice Environment Scale‐Nursing Work Index (PES‐NWI)” and the “Medical Error Attitude Scale”.

pmc-13376115.title: KIF23 in disease pathogenesis and its therapeutic and diagnostic potential
pmc-13376115.creator: Chunmiao Luo, Fuxing Qin, Dunwei Yao, Qiucui Ma, Minzhen Qin, Fong Fong Liew
pmc-13376115.description: BackgroundKinesin family member 23 (KIF23) is a microtubule-dependent motor protein essential for cytokinesis, organelle transport, and signaling pathway regulation. Its dysregulation contributes to both tumorigenesis and non-malignant disorders; however, a comprehensive review integrating recent mechanistic and translational insights is currently lacking.

pmc-13523928.title: Microbiome-mediated regulation of pathogen virulence: Molecular mechanisms and clinical implications
pmc-13523928.creator: Ahmed J Alzahrani
pmc-13523928.description: The human microbiome profoundly influences pathogen virulence and disease susceptibility through diverse molecular mechanisms. This review, focused on literature from 2016 to 2026, synthesizes knowledge on microbiome-mediated regulation examining major pathogens including Vibrio cholerae, enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli, Salmonella species, Clostridioides difficile, and Staphylococcus aureus.

pmc-13579673.title: Mass casualty training for prehospital and emergency providers in Kigali, Rwanda: a quasi-experimental pre–post educational study
pmc-13579673.creator: Oriane Longerstaey, Rafael Davis, William Mullen, Pascal Mugemangango, Kyle Denison Martin
pmc-13579673.description: BackgroundA mass casualty incident (MCI) occurs when the number of patients exceeds available healthcare resources, placing significant strain on prehospital and facility-based emergency care systems, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). An effective response to MCIs requires coordinated systems, targeted training, and clear communication across all levels of care.

uslaw-usc-t42-s14923.title: 42 U.S.C. § 14923 — Standards and procedures for providing accreditation or approval
uslaw-usc-t42-s14923.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s14923.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 143 (Intercountry Adoptions); Subchapter II (Provisions Relating To Accreditation And Approval). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In general (1) Promulgation of regulations The Secretary, shall, by regulation, prescribe the standards and procedures to be used by accrediting entities for the accreditation of agencies and the approval of persons to provide.
